state:
Goal `core-zip` is reached: `bun nv proofs --verify --group 'Core\Zip'` owes nothing and every attack passes with no `proof: gap` marker.
The depth finding is fixed rather than recorded: the reader refuses an entry nesting more than `MAX_FOLDERS` (64) folders, so every member refuses it and one entry's extraction cost is a constant (`crates/nvs-stdlib/src/zip.rs`'s module doc, *That order costs time quadratic*). The gap record is deleted, and `bun nv owners --deferrals` is green again.
The bound is pinned by `tests/conformance/core/zip-refuses-an-entry-nesting-more-than-sixty-four-folders.nvst` and the Rust test `an_entry_nesting_more_than_sixty_four_folders_is_refused`.

items.text: **Make `extract` linear in folder depth** — the reader bounds the folders a name may nest, at `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/zip.rs:398`, judged in `refuse_hostile` at `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/zip.rs:637` (`rule:testing/a-failing-proof-is-fixed-or-recorded`).

backlog: A walk relative to each level's directory handle (`openat`/`mkdirat`, a `RootDirectory` handle on Windows) would also close the window between the last resolution and the file's creation; the capability layer checks paths only, so it needs a design first (`crates/nvs-stdlib/src/zip.rs` module doc).
